proof.text: For the underlying abelian sheaf of an $A_S$-module $M$, [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-stalk] supplies the natural additive comparison $(t^{-1}M)_u\cong M_{tu}$ with no extra hypothesis on $t$. To check its normalization, write $P=u_{t,p}M$ for the presheaf colimit in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. By [lem-cbc-proetale-sheafification-geometric-stalk], $P_u\to(P^\#)_u=(t^{-1}M)_u$ is an isomorphism, so representatives may be computed before sheafification. The double-colimit calculation of Tag 0F4F sends $(U,u',V,\theta,a)$ to $(V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u',a)$. It respects both restriction relations: restriction in $U$ precomposes $u'$, and restriction along $b:V\to V'$ replaces the section by $M(b)(a')$ and the lift by $bw$. The reverse sends $(V,w,a)$ to $(T\times_SV,(u,w),V,\mathrm{id},a)$. The first composite is the identity; for the other composite, $\theta:(U,u')\to(T\times_SV,(u,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u'))$ is a pointed morphism and gives exactly the required colimit relation. These are the maps of the canonical comparison in Tag 05V1. Applying the same formulas to the module action preserves constant scalar sections. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] extension along the coefficient identification transports the action without changing the underlying sheaf, so the comparison for $t^*M$ is $A$-linear. In Lean, first identify the underlying mate of the supplied module adjunction unit. Use the proved ringUnitComparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], which combines canonical module inverse image with uniqueness of left adjoints and the coefficient scalar equivalence, to show that mate is invertible. Transport the abelian stalk comparison through that mate. The inverse germ formula follows from compatibility of the adjunction units; the forward formula follows by restriction along the represented pointed arrow. Filtered-colimit representatives and the constant-section coefficient map prove A-linearity, and the inverse germ formula proves uniqueness.

proof.text: The representative formulas are natural in M: a sheaf map applies to the section a and commutes with both restrictions, while the pointed morphisms are unchanged. For the identity morphism use the normalized identity-pullback comparison. Restricting its unit along the diagonal gives the inverse comparison. Apply the inverse germ formula, the forward germ formula, and the diagonal projection identity; colimit extensionality gives the stated identity-pullback equation with its point transport. Naturality of the module stalk construction in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] then gives the natural-isomorphism equation, and the complex version is termwise.

proof.text: Let $h:Z\to Y$ and $f:Y\to X$ be composable. The direct constant-section identification for $fh$ agrees with the composite identifications: both send every constant $a$ to $a$, and maps out of the sheafification of the constant presheaf are determined by those sections, as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Apply the representative formula of Step 1 first to the comparison for $h$ and then to the comparison for $f$. The two successive base-change objects are canonically identified with the single object $Z\times_XV$ by the associativity and universal property of fibre products; under this identification both composites send a representative to the same germ $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u',a]$ at $fhv$. The comparison $\chi_{h,f}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] is, on a K-flat complex with flat terms, the termwise canonical module-pullback map, so its stalk is precisely the reassociation used here. Therefore the displayed composition identity holds on representatives and is natural in $M$. In Lean, use proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition_ordinary from [lem-trf-derived-pullback-coherence]. It supplies an abstract ordinary comparison with its unit-section formula and identifies its exact-derived image with the prescribed compositor. Apply that formula to the inverse stalk germs, then use two forward germ formulas and the fibre-product projection identity. This avoids unfolding the uniquely normalized comparison witnesses.

proof.text: For $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$, precomposition by $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ sends a pointed neighbourhood $(V,w)$ of $u$ to $(V,w\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha))$ of $u\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)$ and leaves the section unchanged. It preserves the pointed-morphism relation in the colimit, hence induces $r_{u,\alpha,M}([V,w,a])=[V,w\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),a]$. Precomposition by $\alpha^{-1}$ is its inverse, and the same representative calculation proves $A$-linearity and naturality. Applying this reparametrization to the two sides of the Step 1 comparison gives the stated equality for $r$.

proof.text: The inverse-image functors for the identified constant coefficient sheaves are exact and their derived pullbacks are the termwise functors by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The abelian stalk functors are exact by [lem-cbc-proetale-classical-stalk]; hence their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms (their cohomology is the stalk of the cohomology sheaf). The same holds for fixed-$A$ module sheaves on forgetting the action. Apply Steps 1--4 in every degree of a representative complex: all maps commute with differentials by naturality, so the formulas are equalities of chain maps. The comparison in Step 3 is the normalized derived comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Since quasi-isomorphisms are inverted in the ordinary derived category, the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] carries these natural chain-map equalities to the asserted equalities for bounded derived complexes, with no choice of representative affecting them. The generic exact-derived functor factorization, cocycle, identity and whiskering lemmas descend the proved module equalities directly. The characterization of the ordinary comparison identifies this descent with the prescribed canonical derived compositor.

title: Coherence of finite-coefficient pro-etale pullback stalk comparisons
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $Z\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{f}X$ be morphisms of schemes, with small pro-etale sites and compatible small skeletons and universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the constant coefficient sheaves, their canonical inverse-image identifications preserving constant sections [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and the derived pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For a bounded complex $H$ of $A_X$-module sheaves and a geometric point $v:s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ [def-weil-geometric-point], write $H_u$ for the termwise geometric stalk complex at a geometric point $u$, with stalks as in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a morphism $t:T\to S$, geometric point $u:s\to T$, and coefficient complex $M$ on $S$, there is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism
$$c_{t,u,M}:(Lt^*M)_u\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{tu}.$$
It is the canonical inverse-image stalk comparison, normalized as follows using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: for a sheaf $M$, a representative consists of $a\in M(V)$, a site morphism $\theta:U\to T\times_SV$, and a pointed lift $u':s\to U$ over $u$. Its image is $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u',a]$. The inverse sends $[V,w,a]$ to the pullback-unit section on $T\times_SV$ with pointed lift $(u,w)$.

Let $\chi_{h,f}:L(fh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lf^*$ be the canonical composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Then
$$c_{fh,v,H}=c_{f,hv,H}\circ c_{h,v,Lf^*H}\circ(\chi_{h,f,H})_v.$$
Under the canonical identity-pullback identification, $c_{\mathrm{id},u,H}=\mathrm{id}_{H_u}$. For $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$, let $r_{u,\alpha,M}:M_u\to M_{u\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)}$ send $[V,w,a]$ to $[V,w\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),a]$. Then
$$r_{tu,\alpha,M}\circ c_{t,u,M}=c_{t,u\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),M}\circ r_{u,\alpha,Lt^*M}.$$
These equalities are natural in the coefficient complex and hold in the ordinary derived categories after localization at quasi-isomorphisms.
